_comment: Shared rows for surfaceRefractionBrowserSupported: a user agent, and whether that browser composites an SVG filter named in backdrop-filter.

Read by coui_core (the predicate itself) and by the Chrome probes in tool/parity, which load the shipped Web runtime and host under each user agent and read back what the surface's backdrop-filter became - so a browser the table says cannot draw the filter is handed none, and one it says can is.

renders is true only for Blink. WebKit accepts url() in a backdrop-filter list and then draws nothing for a list that names a filter, the surface's own blur included (Safari 27.0 on macOS, measured in a real window: a pane styled blur(10px) url(#f) from the start leaves the pixels behind it as none does, blur(10px) alone changes them all; a pane that was drawn with its chain first and has the reference appended keeps that layer until the browser builds it again - hidden and shown, or inserted again - and then draws nothing). CSS.supports says true, which is why the answer is read off the user agent. Firefox is recorded as behaving alike and has not been measured.

The user agents are the shapes each engine family sends. The Safari, HeadlessChrome and WebKit 26.6 rows are the strings those browsers reported when measured. Chrome, Edge and Firefox on iOS run WebKit and say CriOS, EdgiOS and FxiOS, none of which contains Chrome/.
